title: cli.json
description: A repo's one CLI and the verbs it offers (PLAN-routing-tree.md §14.8; PLAN-architecture.md §12: every repo has one, `cli-declared` reports a repo without it as a `lag` item). With a store, also the store's file(s), for which the CLI is the only way in; the skeleton setup installs is `{store, cli, verbs: []}`. `read` declares which verbs only read, how to call each with `--json`, the fixture they run on and the fields that may differ between two runs; `repro` runs each twice and compares. `accessor` validates this file against this schema with checkslib/checkjson.py and enforces each `x-rules` id in checkslib/contract.py, then audits that nothing else in the repo names the store. One CLI per repo: a repo with two CLIs over two stores is an open decision (TODO.md).

store.description: Optional: the store, one path or a list of paths or globs, relative to the repo root. Its file may be git-ignored (a database usually is). Absent: the repo keeps no store, and its CLI still declares its verbs.

cli.description: The executable that is the repo's CLI (with a store, the only way into it), relative to the repo root.

verbs.description: The verbs the CLI offers; each must be one `<cli> help` lists. Empty in setup's skeleton (`cli-declared` reports an empty list as a lag).

not_verbs.description: Optional: every other command `<cli> help` lists, each with why a caller may not run it. When present, verbs and not_verbs together are exactly the help's commands (the harness's .claude/cli.json uses it).

read.description: Optional: the read verbs, each run as `<cli> <verb> <args...>` by `repro`, twice, on one scratch copy of `fixture`, and compared after the `volatile` fields are removed.

fixture.description: A folder inside the repo. `repro` copies it once to a scratch folder, runs every verb there (that copy is the working directory) and puts the copy's absolute path wherever `{fixture}` appears in `args` or `env`. Absent: the verbs run in the repo root, and `{fixture}` may not appear.

env.description: Variables set for every run, over the caller's environment (`{fixture}` substituted): how a CLI is pointed at its fixture store.

verbs.description: verb -> how to run it. Each verb is one `verbs` lists.

args.description: The arguments after the verb; they include `--json`.

volatile.description: Fields that may differ between two runs (a time asked for, a duration), removed before the comparison: dot-separated keys from the document's root, `*` for every key of an object or every item of an array (`items.*.seconds`). Each must remove something from at least one of the two runs.

_comment.description: Optional prose for the reader; no check reads it.

x-rules.paths-inside: `cli` and every store path are relative paths inside the repo: not absolute, no `..` segment
x-rules.verb-implemented: every verb is a command `<cli> help` lists (checkslib/helptext.py reads the help)
x-rules.unique: no store path twice, no verb twice
x-rules.not-verbs-exact: with not_verbs: no command is in both verbs and not_verbs, and verbs + not_verbs are exactly the commands `<cli> help` lists, both ways
x-rules.read-declared: with read: it names at least one verb, and every verb it names is one `verbs` lists
x-rules.read-json: with read: every read verb's args include `--json`
x-rules.read-fixture: with read: `fixture`, when given, is a folder inside the repo that exists; `{fixture}` appears in args or env only when `fixture` is given
x-rules.read-env: with read.env: every name is an environment variable name (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`) and none is one the checks runner sets for itself (`CHECKS_*`)
x-rules.volatile-paths: with read: every volatile path is dot-separated non-empty keys, and no path is given twice for one verb
